description.narrative:
Specific Objectives
1. To promote responsible mining, and sustainable trade and investment practices that respect the Environmental, Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (EESCRs) and benefit marginalised communities, citizens of Zimbabwe and other targeted stakeholders by December 2028.
2. To improve the sustainable management of land and natural resources that include forestry, water and wildlife, for the benefit of marginalised communities and citizens in Chiredzi district and Bikita district of Zimbabwe and other stakeholders by December 2028.
3. To advocate for climate justice and just transition for the benefit of marginalised communities in Gutu district and Gwanda district of Zimbabwe and other stakeholders by December 2028.
Expected Outcomes
1. Investment practices/frameworks, business and trade especially in the mining sector, influenced to respect for Environmental, Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (EESCRs).
2. Improved biodiversity protection, land governance, and water justice in Zimbabwe in line with relevant national, regional and international frameworks.
3. Enhanced climate mitigation, adaptation, resilience, climate justice in Zimbabwe, in line with relevant national regional and international frameworks.

ZELO aims to foster responsible mining and sustainable trade practices and investments, promote climate mitigation, adaptation, and justice while, improving biodiversity protection, and land and natural resources governance throughout Zimbabwe and beyond. Expected outcomes include significant improvements in sustainable and equitable natural resource governance, enhanced food security, increased climate resilience, and respect for community and citizen rights, towards a sustainable future.

Zimbabwe Environmental Law Organisation (ZELO), under ett projekt med titeln "Främjande av rättvis och hållbar förvaltning av naturresurser (ProNRM)", syftar till att främja ansvarsfull gruvdrift samt hållbara handelsmetoder och investeringar, främja klimatåtgärder, anpassning och rättvisa, samtidigt som biologisk mångfald skyddas och förvaltningen av mark och naturresurser förbättras i Zimbabwe och bortom dess gränser. Förväntade resultat inkluderar betydande förbättringar i hållbar och rättvis förvaltning av naturresurser, ökad livsmedelssäkerhet, stärkt klimatresiliens och respekt för samhällens och medborgares rättigheter – mot en hållbar framtid.

KEY RESULTS ACHIEVED (August 2025-May 2026)
Outcome 1: Investment practices/frameworks, business and trade, especially in the mining sector, influenced to respect for environmental, economic, social and cultural rights (EESCRs). The project strengthened pathways for responsible and rights-based investment governance in Zimbabwe's extractives sector. ZELO developed a draft due diligence framework aimed at promoting transparency, responsible investment, and sustainable resource governance in the critical minerals sector. The framework, now under consideration by the Zimbabwe Investment Development Agency (ZIDA), provides an important mechanism for aligning domestic investment systems with international ESG standards and strengthening investor accountability.
ZELO also expanded its influence within national and continental investment discourse through convening the Zimbabwe Alternative Mining Indaba (2025) and Alternative Mining Indaba (2026). These engagements elevated discussions on responsible mining and strengthened partnerships with institutions such as ZIDA, MMCZ and Fidelity Printers around integrating ESG standards into investment systems and practices. Importantly, ZELO succeeded in bringing issues of environmental, economic, social and cultural rights (EESCRs) into mainstream investment discussions at the Invest in African Mining Indaba, a platform traditionally dominated by governments, investors and mining companies. This represented an important shift, ensuring that community rights, accountability and responsible investment considerations became part of broader conversations shaping mining investments for the first time
Outcome 2: Improved biodiversity protection, land governance, and water justice in Zimbabwe in line with relevant national, regional and international frameworks.
The project strengthened biodiversity governance and created opportunities for more inclusive and community-centred conservation systems through the development of a draft framework on community conservancy, which established an important foundation for strengthening biodiversity protection and enhancing community participation in natural resource management.
Learning and engagement following participation in the Business of Conservation Congress (BCC) catalysed strategic institutional partnerships and policy discussions around conservation governance. Engagement with the Parks and Wildlife Management Authority (ZimParks) identified priority reform areas around CAMPFIRE governance structures, accountability systems, constitutional alignment and strengthening community-based natural resource management models.
Beyond influencing dialogue, these engagements generated tangible institutional opportunities. ZELO signed an MoU with African Parks in March 2026, through which the organisation was engaged to conduct a human rights impact assessment in Matusadona National Park, where African Parks is programming on conservation issues with communities. This reflected growing recognition of ZELOs expertise and strengthened its role in shaping rights-based approaches to conservation and biodiversity governance.
Outcome 3: Enhanced climate mitigation, adaptation, resilience, and climate justice in Zimbabwe, in line with relevant national, regional and international frameworks.
ZELO strengthened its influence within climate governance and policy processes by contributing to national climate reform discussions and strengthening local adaptation systems. Upon invitation by Parliament, ZELO influenced as a civil society representative in shaping discussions on the Climate Change Management Bill, presenting and advocating for stronger provisions on climate mitigation, incorporation of just energy transition principles, and stronger safeguards around the National Climate Fund. The Bill progressing through its second reading in Parliament reflected growing recognition of ZELO as a credible actor within climate and environmental governance spaces.
At community level, peer learning and institutional strengthening initiatives generated practical pathways for enhancing climate resilience and adaptive capacity. The exchange visits between Ruti and Ranga irrigation schemes, together with reviews of We Effect hubs, strengthened awareness and generated practical recommendations around institutional governance, financial management systems, and climate adaptation planning. Importantly, learning translated into action: following exposure to the Ranga horticulture programme, 40 farmers from Ruti Irrigation Scheme adopted horticultural production within their own fields, initially focusing on crops such as garlic and onions, with seed support provided by Ranga farmers. In a reciprocal learning process, Ranga farmers invited Ruti farmers to support them in strengthening their record-keeping systems, demonstrating emerging peer-to-peer collaboration and knowledge exchange that is strengthening local resilience and community-led adaptation systems.
Source: ProNRM Interim Report Klaradia Reference number: UM2025/16053/HARA/76
